title: Life in the Third Oikos: A Conversation With Leah Libresco Sargeant
gist: Nicole Williams Ruiz interviews Leah Libresco Sargeant (Institute for Progress) on conversion, intentional Catholic community in Hyattsville, dating, and household tech. She would ban dating apps, advises 'VC-style' high-variance dating, runs a bits-vs-atoms division of household labor, and is bearish that remote work yet enables a home-centered 'Third Oikos' economy.

insights.claim: Sargeant argues the most helpful (if unrealistic) fix for falling marriage would be government shutting down dating apps, because their infinite choice cannibalizes better ways of meeting partners through friend networks.
insights.speaker: Leah Libresco Sargeant
insights.so_what: Highlights reputational/regulatory risk narratives around dating platforms.
insights.quote: What I think would help the most but isn’t going to happen—the government seizes and shuts down all dating apps.

insights.claim: For app users she recommends a venture-capitalist approach: make many high-variance bets, avoid bland dates aimed only at securing a second date, and prolong only matches likely to reach a tenth date.
insights.speaker: Leah Libresco Sargeant
insights.so_what: Portfolio framing of mate search; implies apps optimize for the wrong metric.
insights.quote: you've got to treat it like you are a venture capitalist. You're trying to make a lot of bets, most of which won't pan out

insights.claim: She contends events that make people admire each other, like late-night philosophical debates or challenging book and film discussions, beat wine-and-cheese networking for fostering marriages.
insights.speaker: Leah Libresco Sargeant
insights.so_what: Demand signal for curated, interest-dense social formats over generic mixers.
insights.quote: Networking events with cheese and wine are not good for this.

insights.claim: Ruiz states most of the decline in marriage and birth rates appears downstream of people pairing off later and struggling to find partners.
insights.speaker: Nicole Williams Ruiz
insights.so_what: Partner-search friction as the key fertility bottleneck.
insights.locator: Most of the decline in marriage

insights.claim: Hyattsville, Maryland hosts an intentional Catholic community of large families supported by guaranteed meal trains, borrowed tools and children roaming unsupervised between homes.
insights.speaker: Leah Libresco Sargeant
insights.so_what: Example of community-driven location choice for families; local real-estate demand driver.

insights.claim: A weekly mothers' Rosary group surfaces private hardships such as repeated miscarriages, showing prayer-based communities generate intimacy that ordinary social groups lack.
insights.speaker: Leah Libresco Sargeant
insights.so_what: Social-support mechanisms that secular alternatives struggle to replicate.
insights.quote: You get this real intimacy from a community rooted in prayer

insights.claim: Sargeant built a browser extension with Claude Code that delays Twitter by about 20 seconds and shows a prayer request before loading.
insights.speaker: Leah Libresco Sargeant
insights.so_what: Non-programmers using AI coding tools to build personal attention-management tools.
insights.quote: I built, using Claude Code, an extension for my web browser that delays Twitter when I open it.

insights.claim: She finds grayscale phone screens ineffective and argues reducing screen use depends mainly on compelling alternatives such as library e-books, walks and print newspapers, plus keeping the TV in a locked basement.
insights.speaker: Leah Libresco Sargeant
insights.so_what: Friction and substitutes, not settings, drive digital-wellbeing behavior.
insights.quote: But I think it's mostly about having compelling alternatives.

insights.claim: Sargeant describes a 'bits vs atoms' household division in which she handles digital and administrative tasks while her husband handles physical ones, framing differing task aversions as gains from trade.
insights.speaker: Leah Libresco Sargeant
insights.quote: It's great when you and your spouse have different tastes in tasks.

insights.claim: Ruiz's publication theses that post-AI, post-digital technology will move production back into the home, and she believes society is at the cusp of that transition.
insights.speaker: Nicole Williams Ruiz
insights.so_what: Bull case for home-based production enabled by AI.
insights.quote: our post-industrial society—the Third Oikos, the imagination of this post-AI, post-digital-technology society—will enable production to move back into the home

insights.claim: Sargeant is more bearish on the Third Oikos arriving soon: hybrid work (three office days, two remote) does not translate into flexibility at home because child care schedules remain rigid.
insights.speaker: Leah Libresco Sargeant
insights.so_what: Remote work gains for families are capped by inflexible child care; childcare flexibility is the binding constraint.
insights.quote: I’m more bearish on how close we are to the Third Oikos
